title: Expectation and Linearity
quickIdea: Expectation is the probability-weighted average of the values, and it is linear: averages of sums are sums of averages, always, with no independence needed.
remember: Discrete: E[X] = the sum of x P(X = x) over the values. Continuous: E[X] = the integral of x f(x) dx.
E[g(X)] = the sum (or integral) of g(x) times the probability (or density) - you never need the distribution of g(X) to average g(X).
Linearity: E[aX + b] = a E[X] + b, and E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] for any two variables, dependent or not.
The expectation need not be a value the variable can take: a fair die has E[X] = 3.5.
Check that the probabilities sum to 1 before averaging; the Hindi page lists exactly this as the first common mistake, and it is the cheapest check in the exam.

The mean of a symmetric distribution is its centre of symmetry, so for the uniform it is (a + b)/2, for the normal it is mu, and for the exponential it is 1/lambda - all of which follow from the definition rather than being separate facts.

example.prompt: X takes the values 1 to 8 with P(1) = P(2) = P(5) = P(7) = 1/6 and P(3) = P(4) = P(6) = P(8) = 1/12. Find E[X].
example.work: Group the two kinds of value: E[X] = (1/6)(1 + 2 + 5 + 7) + (1/12)(3 + 4 + 6 + 8) = 15/6 + 21/12 = 2.5 + 1.75 = 4.25. The check: four values at 1/6 and four at 1/12 give 4/6 + 4/12 = 2/3 + 1/3 = 1, so the table is a distribution.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.48 is this computation, and the marks are lost by adding the eight values and dividing by 8 - that gives 4.5, the answer for the uniform distribution on the same support, not for this one. The grouping shortcut (equal probabilities collected first) is what makes it a one-minute question.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.48: X takes values in {1,...,8} with P(1) = P(2) = P(5) = P(7) = 1/6 and P(3) = P(4) = P(6) = P(8) = 1/12. The expected value E[X] is ______ (two decimal places).
variations.why: E[X] = 15/6 + 21/12 = 51/12 = 4.25. The answer 4.5 is the trap: it is the mean of the uniform distribution on {1,...,8}, which this is not, since the eight values do not carry equal probability.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: X takes the value 0 with probability 0.5, 1 with probability 0.3 and 2 with probability 0.2. Find E[X] and E[3X + 4].
variations.why: E[X] = 0(0.5) + 1(0.3) + 2(0.2) = 0.7. By linearity E[3X + 4] = 3(0.7) + 4 = 6.1, which is faster than recomputing the distribution of 3X + 4, and the two routes must agree.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Two variables have E[X] = 2 and E[Y] = 5 and are not independent. What is E[X + Y]?
variations.why: Linearity of expectation needs no independence. Only multiplicative statements such as E[XY] = E[X]E[Y], and the addition of variances, need it. GATE has used this distinction to build options that are true for independent variables only.

trap.what: Averaging the values without their probabilities, or dividing by the count of values instead of weighting.
trap.why: The distribution is a weighting, not a list. Treating the values as equally likely silently replaces the question with a different one.
trap.counterexample: For the 2026 Set 1 distribution, the unweighted average of 1 to 8 is 4.5, while the correct expectation is 4.25. The two differ exactly because the four small probabilities sit on the larger values 3, 4, 6 and 8, pulling the mean down.
